content.text: {"primary_meaning":"A divinely prepared way by which God comes to his people and leads the redeemed into salvation, holiness, restoration, and ultimately his presence.","primary_basis":["Isaiah 35:8–10 — the “Highway of Holiness” is the safe way traveled by the redeemed returning to Zion.","Isaiah 40:3–5 — a way is prepared in the wilderness for the coming of the Lord; applied to John the Baptist’s preparation for Christ in Matthew 3:3, Mark 1:2–3, Luke 3:4–6, and John 1:23.","Isaiah 11:15–16 — a highway enables the remnant to return in a new-exodus restoration.","Isaiah 49:11–12 — God turns obstacles into roads for the gathering of his people.","Isaiah 62:10–12 — the highway is prepared and cleared for the salvation and return of God’s people."],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"The path of righteous or upright conduct, contrasted with sinful, obstructed, or destructive ways.","basis":["Proverbs 15:19 — the way of the upright is a highway.","Proverbs 16:17 — the highway of the upright turns away from evil.","Isaiah 35:8 — the Highway of Holiness also supports an ethical or sanctification-focused reading."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Eschatological reconciliation and free communion among formerly hostile peoples under God’s rule.","basis":["Isaiah 19:23–25 — a highway joins Egypt and Assyria, and both worship with Israel."],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"A route for the gathering of nations or exiles, emphasizing removal of barriers and universal access to God’s restored people.","basis":["Isaiah 11:16","Isaiah 19:23","Isaiah 49:11–12","Isaiah 62:10"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"A literal public road or raised roadway, without an independent symbolic meaning.","basis":["In several biblical contexts, the word denotes an actual road or route; its figurative significance must be determined from the immediate passage."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"An opened route for military advance, conquest, or judgment rather than salvation.","basis":["Some prophetic road imagery concerns the approach of armies or divine judgment, making the highway an image of unobstructed access rather than inherently of redemption."],"prominence":"minority"}],"has_settled_consensus":false,"confidence":"high","notes":"Christian interpretation strongly associates highway imagery—especially in Isaiah—with preparation for God’s coming and the redeemed people’s return, salvation, and holiness.
